clue.text: Long novel I read initially back in first school group?

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: the top stream of a school year is Class A

indicators.note: back says the two letters before it are taken in the reverse order
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word read

explanation.surface: A long novel is read in a first-year school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns I and R into RI, which goes inside CLASS A to give CLA-RI-SSA. CLARISSA is Samuel Richardson's very long 18th-century novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Richardson's epistolary Clarissa is among the longest novels in English, a fair example of a long book.

clue.text: Lines about award I advanced? That's a bloomer

indicators.note: the two line letters go around the award, holding it between them

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so lines doubles it
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Someone talks of advancing an award, then admits the slip-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, the British sense of a mistake, but here it is literally something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobelia is a flowering garden plant, so it is a bloomer in the sense of a thing that flowers.

clue.text: Prophet, upset about me blocking some work, appears again

indicators.note: the reversed me and the work unit sit inside the prophet word, blocking it
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the prophet word reads backwards

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so me is read backwards

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A prophet, offended by some piece of work, makes a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the prophet to REES and 'about' turns me round; that pair plus the work unit goes 'blocking', splitting REES in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-emerge is to come out into view once more, so a person doing it appears again.

clue.text: Little dispute about river fish

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes around the river letter

parts.note: a spat is a small quarrel

explanation.surface: A minor squabble about where to catch fish on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The sprat is a small silvery sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Decide not to choose one covered in muscles (bronzed)

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

indicators.note: the numeral one is wrapped up inside the word for bronzed

parts.note: bronzed skin is tanned, giving tan
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tanned, muscular person refuses to make a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts the one inside the bronzed word; 'Decide not to choose' is the definition, as when one declines to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain in a vote is to decline to pick any option.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument fixed with insertion of peg

indicators.note: the peg word is placed inside the word for fixed

parts.note: set means fixed or settled
a pin is a peg

explanation.surface: A keyboard instrument mended by inserting a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinet is a small harpsichord-like instrument played from a keyboard.

clue.text: Abuse of justice — this row upset almost everyone

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters of this row are knocked into a new order
almost drops the final letter of the word for everyone

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody is upset by this quarrel over a miscarriage of justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges THIS ROW to SHOWTRI; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A show trial is a staged trial with a predetermined verdict, a perversion of justice for propaganda.

clue.text: African country elevated about introduction of state religion

indicators.note: the reversed country goes around the chosen letter
in a down clue elevated means lifted up, so the country is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: introduction of points to the opening letter of state

explanation.surface: An African nation promotes its state religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns MALI into ILAM, which wraps S.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith founded by the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Horse rider always circling Tolkien creature

indicators.note: the word for always goes round the Tolkien creature

parts.note: ever means always
Ents are the tree-like giants of The Lord of the Rings

explanation.surface: A rider forever riding round one of Tolkien's beings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer competes in equestrian eventing: dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Obscure leader of Britons, character in play

indicators.note: leader of takes the front letter of Britons

parts.note: King Lear is the title character of Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A shadowy ancient British leader appearing as a stage character.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear was a legendary king of the Britons, so the surface hangs together; 'Obscure' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To blear is to blur or dim, especially the eyes or vision, so it means to obscure.

clue.text: Source of information, special, also misinformation

parts.note: too means also
a lie is false information

explanation.surface: An informant whose special reports are also full of falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoolie, short for stool pigeon, is a police informer, a person who supplies information.

clue.text: Glib Fellow advanced, taking in university

indicators.note: the word for advanced holds the university letter inside it

parts.note: advanced money is lent

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking academic fellow lends money while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib speech flows easily and smoothly, a near synonym of articulate and smooth-tongued.

clue.text: A fellow keeping out revolutionary change to involve machinery

indicators.note: the a-plus-fellow pair keeps the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion

indicators.note: revolutionary signals the letters of out are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A colleague shuts out a radical figure in a change towards mechanisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges the word out to UTO; 'keeping' means it sits inside the a-plus-fellow pair, just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To automate a process is to convert it so that machines do the work.

clue.text: Irritation suppressed by dear follower

indicators.note: the irritation word is held down inside the endearment

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is an endearment like dear
anger is irritation or annoyance

explanation.surface: A devoted admirer hides annoyance from a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who attaches themselves to someone important.

clue.text: One can become upset after others curtailed sympathetic reaction

indicators.note: after places the shuffled letters behind the trimmed word
curtailed cuts off the tail, so the last letter of the others word goes

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: become upset signals the letters of one can are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone becomes upset after the rest are cut short, a sympathetic response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims REST to RES; 'become upset' rearranges ONE CAN to ONANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics resonance is vibration induced in sympathy with another, so it is a sympathetic reaction.

clue.text: Cut short person you want to avoid in pub? Perfectly natural

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: cut short drops the final letter

parts.note: a bore is a tedious person one avoids, especially in a pub

explanation.surface: Cutting short the pub bore is only natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' trims BORE to BOR, which goes 'in' INN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inborn trait is innate, present from birth, hence natural rather than learned.

clue.text: Two items of data hardware right for transport operator

parts.note: a bus carries data in a computer and a drive stores it

explanation.surface: Computer hardware is the right tool for a transport company.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus driver operates a public passenger vehicle, so runs transport.

clue.text: Appearances — I guess — may be deceptive

indicators.note: deceptive signals the letters of I guess are disguised in a new order

explanation.surface: A play on the saying that appearances can be deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Guises are outward forms or semblances, often assumed to conceal the truth.

clue.text: Pointless blowing top about one's exploit

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes around the letters for one's
blowing top loses the top letter, the first in a down clue

parts.note: futile means pointless
one is I, and one's is I plus S for is

explanation.surface: Losing your temper over someone's heroic exploit is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing top' leaves UTILE; 'one's' is read as 'one is', and 'about' wraps the trimmed word around those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a resource is to make use of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Who could be first and foremost in manipulating LA?

definitions.text: Who could be first and foremost in manipulating LA?

indicators.note: could be signals the letters that follow may be made into something else, a new order
foremost in takes the opening letter of manipulating

explanation.surface: Who is the top person pulling the strings in Los Angeles?
explanation.walkthrough: FIRST, the M from 'foremost in manipulating', and LA are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer, a Hollywood celebrity at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A top screen actor is the leading figure in Hollywood, a Los Angeles district.

clue.text: Flower is picked up in open area

indicators.note: the lifted word sits inside the open-plus-area letters

parts.note: free means open, unrestricted

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so is is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A flower is gathered in an open space.
explanation.definitionFit: The freesia is a fragrant South African plant grown for its blooms.

clue.text: Substantial distress comes in the wake of a girl

indicators.note: the big and distress words follow behind the letter a

parts.note: big means substantial
to ail is to trouble or distress

explanation.surface: Great distress follows a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a girl's given name and, by tradition, a term for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Line adopted by one injured in crime such as GBH?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the crime word

parts.note: vice is wickedness or criminal activity

indicators.note: the line letter is taken into the word one
injured signals the combined letters are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: An injured victim of a violent assault adopts a line of defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges the line-in-one letters to OLEN, put 'in' the crime word. GBH, grievous bodily harm, is a serious assault charge in British law.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous bodily harm is an example of violent crime, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Learner in game of skill finds jargon

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
Go is the ancient East Asian board game of strategy

explanation.surface: A beginner playing a skilful game picks up its specialist vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for the specialist vocabulary of a group, i.e. jargon.

clue.text: Lake I located in one capital city or another

indicators.note: the lake letter and I are placed inside the first capital

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: A lake found in one capital or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: putting L and I inside one capital (BERN) gives another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the German capital, a second capital besides Switzerland's.

clue.text: Note girl's date's almost tardy

parts.note: BF is short for boyfriend, the one a girl dates

indicators.note: almost removes the end letter of the tardy word

parts.note: late means tardy

explanation.surface: A note that a girl's date is running a bit late.
explanation.definitionFit: B flat is a musical note, a semitone below B.

clue.text: Prize after missing first place in a bit of sporting endeavour

indicators.note: missing first place drops the opening letter

parts.note: winnings are prize money

explanation.surface: A prize when you miss out on first in a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is a batting turn in cricket or baseball, one session of the game.

clue.text: Roman matriarch, endlessly angry one

indicators.note: endlessly cuts off the last letter of the angry word

parts.note: livid means furious
a means one

explanation.surface: A furious Roman mother figure, never stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Livia, wife of Augustus and mother of Tiberius, was the founding matriarch of imperial Rome's first dynasty.

clue.text: Suit company with millions invested in competitive group

indicators.note: the company and millions letters are put inside the group word

parts.note: a bee is a gathering for a contest, as in a spelling bee
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A firm puts millions into a competitive syndicate, sharp suit and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing but is the verb: a hat may become you.
explanation.definitionFit: To become someone is to flatter or look good on them, as clothes suit a wearer.

clue.text: It describes most of the dictionary, in spite of everything

definitions.text: It describes most of the dictionary
definitions.meaning: most dictionary entries come alphabetically later than the letters A and L

explanation.surface: A wry remark that, despite all, most of a dictionary is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the phrase puts most words alphabetically past 'AL', the start of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless or when everything is considered.
